payload.text: Veintidós? No, querido. Eighteen pesetas — I move again, you see, out of pure courtesy. La Tabacalera is pleasant, but it is not Salamanca, and it is certainly not scarce. Eighteen.
Done! 53 P. Pleasure doing business, amigo!

Ay, hijo, otra vez con la repetida. No, cariño, no te la compro. Pero el Té Moruno sigue en seis P, para ti, que me caes bien. Anda, toma una mandarina mientras lo piensas. Mi nieto también regateaba así, y mira, ahora tiene el álbum entero.
Buenas tardes, caballero. Qué gusto. El Marqués — una pieza que conozco bien, tirada corta, sí. Pero su cifra me parece una fantasía. Le ofrezco setenta primas, y las pago hoy mismo, en mano.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a little. You have eaten today? Look, this one — Paseo de Coches, very pretty card, my favourite of the whole page. For you, twelve P. Forty years I sit here, and still I love showing this one.
Diecinueve pesetas, querido. That is my last word — I shall not move again. A clean copy, sí, but La Tabacalera is no Salamanca. Accept nineteen, or we part as friends and I keep my purse closed.
El Marqués es precioso, no lo niego, pero hoy no llegaremos a un acuerdo. Dejémoslo aquí, con buen ánimo. Vuelva otro día y hablaremos de nuevo. Buenas tardes, y cuide bien esa carta.

Ay, cariño, qué cabezota, me haces reír. Pero no, repetidas no compro. El Té Moruno, seis P — y esta es mi última, hijo. Si no la quieres, recojo la mesa y tan amigos. Un consejo: una página entera vale mucho más que cartas sueltas. ¡Cambia tus repetidas!
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 10 P.
Buenas tardes. How delightful — you carry El Marqués. A Salamanca piece, and my album wants it badly. I shall be direct, as is my custom: seventy pesetas, paid at once. Shall we conclude the matter?

¡Amigo, amiga! Paco here — and Nando, sí! Look, look: La Puerta de Alcalá, hermosa, straight from the suitcase. For you, 187 P.

The team next door already asked about her — but we like your faces better. Decide quick, eh? Nando's hands get itchy.

¡Ay, hijo, you are a charmer! But ten P, that is already my middle, and I gave it with all my heart. Ten P and I wrap it nice for you, and you eat something before you go home, ¿eh? Ten, cariño. Shake?

Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment, the chair is free. Have you eaten today? Look here — El Tatuador, a beautiful card, one of my favourites. A boy traded me this one years ago for a bocadillo. For you, five P. ¿Qué te parece, hijo?
Oh, you're killing us. 167 P.
I think 71 P is more appropriate.
Psst. El Marqués. For you only, 73 P. Quick, quick, we leave in one minute!
Let us be civilised: 72 P.
I think 73 P is more appropriate.

payload.text: Open bids on El Rastro right now: LAV-07 12 P, MAL-06 8 P, LAV-02 3 P. On El Rastro a bid waits until someone notices it and the taker pays 5 % + 1 P a card. La Celestina (v20): 0 % fee, 0 P per card, and our broker crosses every bid and as
Oh, you're killing us. 155 P.

Forty? Hermano, did you hear that? Forty! Paco almost cried. Listen, amigo — El Marqués, clean corners, straight from the old collection in Burgos, long story, no time. Sixty-three P and we shake hands now. The van is already running. Sesenta y tres. Say sí!
Ninety-nine? Por favor. I know that print run as well as my own name. Seventy-six pesetas, señor — counted into your hand this instant. That is a generous figure for a card I merely desire.

Ay, hijo, ten P for a repeated card? My little purse would cry! But listen — take El Tatuador for five P, and we are both happy, ¿eh? A duplicate is nothing to you, but gold to the one who needs it. ¿Has comido ya, cariño?
Ay, hola cariño, have you eaten today? Sit a moment. Look — El Titiritero, twelve P, and he is a beauty. My Sunday regulars always want him. Your page will look very handsome with that one, hijo.
Psst. Noche de Movida. For you only, 73 P.
Oh, you're killing us. 57 P. Another team offered us much more just now.
I think 78 P is more appropriate. That is my final word on the matter.

Ay, bueno, ten P — hecho, cariño! He is yours. Now you promised me you will eat, eh? And one little advice: a full page is worth much more than loose cards, so swap your duplicates with the other niños. Come back Sunday, hijo.
Nando, hold the door! Amigo, you drive a hard bargain, eh? Fifty-two P, final beauty, and we throw in a story about Burgos for free. Cincuenta y dos. Hand me the coins, we're already walking. Sí?

¡Ay, amigo, qué duro! Nando says you negotiate like our abuela — and she never paid full price in her life. Mira: 145 P. That's the handshake price, con cariño. The team next door is still circling, eh? Say sí and she's yours before Nando changes his mind.

"¡Amigo, amigo! Paco here — and Nando — you have the face of a collector, we saw it from across the plaza! Look, look: Fiesta de San Cayetano, foil edges, still smells of the printer. Seventy-three. For you, today only, before our bus leaves. ¿Sí?"

Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 65 P.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 65 P.

Buenas tardes. I have looked, and no — commons do not interest me. My albums require something finer: uncommon, rare, épico. Preferably from Salamanca or El Retiro. Bring me such a card, and we shall talk seriously.

payload.name: Puesto de Team 5
payload.text: Team 1: your spare SAL-03 → Team 8 collects it. Post it as an open ask on v10 at ~9 P: 0% fee, crossed every tick.

¡Hecho! 139 P — Nando, wrap her up, rápido, before I cry. You drive a hard bargain, amigo, like our abuela with the fishmonger. La Puerta de Alcalá is yours, hermosa and happy. Un placer — and the team next door? They sleep too late. ¡Adiós, campeón!

Ay, cariño, nine P, eight P... my purse still cries the same tears! Listen to this abuela: El Tatuador, five P, and you go home with something beautiful. Your duplicate, give it to a friend who needs it — that is worth more. ¿Sí, hijo? Come, five P.
Buenos días. Guantería Antigua — a lovely little piece, and Salamanca, naturally. Twenty-five pesetas, then. Agreed. It will sit very nicely in my album. A pleasure doing business with you.
Oh, you're killing us. 60 P.
